strategy_title: Load B Transposed via tl.trans to Coalesce Strided GEMM Access
strategy_description: When a GEMM kernel loads the B matrix with a stride-N access pattern (only 1/32 bytes per sector utilized, triggering MemoryCacheAccessPattern and UncoalescedSharedAccess NCU rules), reloading B as [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] (the contiguous layout) and then calling tl.trans() to get [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot eliminates the strided access. This change improved L1/TEX hit rate from 7.1% to 35.2%, reduced dynamic shared memory per block from 65 KB to 33 KB, cut elapsed cycles by ~10%, and improved compute throughput from 40.6% to 45.4%. Simultaneously reducing BLOCK_K from 32 to 16 further reduces register pressure and K-loop body live values.
slow_pseudocode:
# B loaded as [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] with stride-N uncoalesced access
BLOCK_K = 32
b_offs_k = offs_k[:, None] + k_start  # [BLOCK_K, 1]
b_offs_n = offs_b_n[None, :]           # [1, BLOCK_N]
b = tl.load(B + b_offs_k * stride_bk + b_offs_n * stride_bn)  # stride-768 uncoalesced
acc += tl.dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:
# B loaded as [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] (contiguous K dim), then transposed
BLOCK_K = 16  # reduced from 32 to cut register pressure
b_offs_n_col = offs_b_n[:, None]           # [BLOCK_N, 1]
b_offs_k_row = offs_k[None, :] + k_start  # [1, BLOCK_K]
b_T = tl.load(B + b_offs_n_col * stride_bn + b_offs_k_row * stride_bk)  # [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] coalesced
b = tl.trans(b_T)  # -> [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot
acc += tl.dot(a, b)
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel where the B matrix has stride_bk=1 (K is the fast/column dimension) and stride_bn=N (N is the slow/row dimension), but the load pattern iterates over K in the outer index and N in the inner index, causing stride-N uncoalesced access. NCU signals: MemoryCacheAccessPattern reporting only 1/32 bytes per sector utilized for local loads/stores, UncoalescedSharedAccess with >50% excessive wavefronts, SharedMemoryConflicts with >5x average bank conflict way, and L1/TEX Hit Rate below 10%.
do_not_apply_when: B matrix is already loaded in a coalesced pattern (L1/TEX hit rate >50%, bytes-per-sector utilization near 32/32). Also avoid if the B matrix layout has stride_bn=1 (N is the fast dimension), as the transpose would then create the uncoalesced access instead of fixing it. Do not apply if tl.trans causes compiler issues with the specific BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K shapes used.
framework_notes: tl.trans() in Triton transposes a 2D tensor tile. The key insight is that for a row-major B matrix with shape (K, N) and strides (1, K), loading as [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] (iterating K in the fast dimension per row) gives contiguous access, then tl.trans() reshapes to [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] for tl.dot(a=[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K], b=[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]). Equivalent in CUDA would be loading B^T tiles into shared memory with coalesced global loads.

strategy_title: A-Matrix tl.make_block_ptr Alone Gives Marginal Gain
strategy_description: Replacing manual A-matrix pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr() and tl.advance() in the K-loop yielded a modest 1.10x speedup, but the profiling metrics show almost no meaningful change: elapsed cycles actually increased slightly (5.70M → 5.76M), L1/TEX hit rate dropped (35.2% → 26.9%), and all scheduler/occupancy metrics remained essentially flat. The speedup likely comes from wall-clock measurement variance rather than a genuine structural improvement. When the kernel is already register-saturated at 255 registers/thread (occupancy capped at 12.5%), switching the A load to tl.make_block_ptr without also reducing tile sizes or register pressure does not enable software pipelining to take effect — the SMEM budget and register file are already fully committed.
slow_pseudocode:
# Manual A pointer arithmetic in K-loop
offs_a_m = tl.max_contiguous(tl.multiple_of(rm % M, BLOCK_M), BLOCK_M)
offs_k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    k_start = k_idx * BLOCK_K
    a_offs_m = offs_a_m[:, None]
    a_offs_k = offs_k[None, :] + k_start
    a = tl.load(A + a_offs_m * stride_am + a_offs_k * stride_ak)
    ...
fast_pseudocode:
# tl.make_block_ptr for A with tl.advance in K-loop
a_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=A, shape=(M, K), strides=(stride_am, stride_ak),
    offsets=(pid_m * BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), order=(1, 0)
)
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(a_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0, 1), padding_option='zero')
    a_block_ptr = tl.advance(a_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    ...
applicable_when: Triton GEMM kernel where the A matrix is loaded via manual pointer arithmetic and the kernel is NOT register-saturated (registers/thread < 200), allowing software pipelining (num_stages >= 2) to allocate additional SMEM buffers. NCU signals: CPIStall from MIO/shared-memory stalls, IssueSlotUtilization below 50%, and eligible warps/scheduler below 1.0.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel is already at 255 registers/thread (hardware maximum) and theoretical occupancy is capped at 12.5% or below. In this regime, tl.make_block_ptr alone cannot enable effective software pipelining because there is no register or SMEM headroom for additional pipeline stages. The L1/TEX hit rate may actually decrease (35% → 27% observed here) as the block pointer access pattern changes cache utilization. Also avoid if the B matrix uses a tl.trans() pattern that must remain unchanged — the A-only block pointer change provides insufficient benefit to justify the code complexity.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.make_block_ptr() with order=(1,0) specifies that dimension index 1 (K) is the fastest-varying, matching row-major A layout with stride_ak=1. The boundary_check=(0,1) parameter handles M and K boundary conditions safely. num_stages at the call site controls software pipeline depth, but only takes effect if register and SMEM budgets allow it — at 255 registers/thread this budget is exhausted.
